hints.title: De Bruijn Graph
hints.text: The shortest sequence containing all k^n substrings is an Eulerian path on a directed graph whose vertices are prefixes of length n minus one.

hints.title: Edge Directed Transitions
hints.text: From vertex node of length n minus one, transitioning on digit x leads to next vertex node[1:] + x, visiting the n-length sequence node + x.

hints.title: Hierholzer Algorithm
hints.text: Run post-order DFS to find an Eulerian circuit starting at "0" times (n - 1). Traverse outgoing edges 0 through k minus one, recording digits in post-order and appending the starting prefix.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Eulerian path construction over De Bruijn graph with k^(n-1) nodes and k^n edges.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy search without Eulerian circuit logic can get trapped before visiting all k^n combinations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking visited edges in a hash set runs in linear time relative to the optimal sequence length.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Model states as length (n-1) suffixes and recognize the De Bruijn Eulerian traversal.
